chapters.title: The Home That Moves
chapters.setting: the steppe-to-Gobi edge, a herding camp at dawn; present day
beats: Cold open keystone image: a herding family strikes the ger at dawn to follow the grass — the whole felt home folded onto a few animals in under an hour, a thousand-year choreography
On the ridge, a new mining-lease fence cuts the migration route the grandfather rode — the home that moves meeting a line that doesn't
Establish Tuyaa watching from a survey vehicle, notebook of the consultancy's language in her lap, the steppe she fled pulling at her
Plant her two worlds: the city smoke she came from, the grass sea she left; the shame under the cynicism
chapters.turn: Tuyaa realises the camp being struck is her own father's — she has been sent home and didn't know it would be HOME
chapters.threads: NODE: arrival / the empty story. Tuyaa lead established; the fence (threat) and the migration (wonder) in one picture.

chapters.title: The Acceptable Face
chapters.setting: the survey camp; the district sum centre; present day
beats: Tuyaa's brief made explicit: she is the Mongolian, daughter-of-herders face for a copper-and-water survey meant to reframe the steppe as 'underused frontier' and grease the lease
She tells herself it's the humane version — better her than a stranger
Introduce the mine's fixer: reasonable, Mongolian, sincere about development, frames the herders as the past
The visiting crew arrives for a parallel commission — a 'timeless Genghis-land' travelogue — the soft version of the same erasure
chapters.turn: Tuyaa sees that her survey and the crew's travelogue are the same erasure wearing two faces; she says nothing
chapters.threads: NODE: the flattening force shows its face. The fixer + the crew introduced; both commissions are the lie.

chapters.title: The Crew
chapters.setting: the road in; the survey camp; present day
beats: Introduce the crew from the inside (Naila's close third): the band of the world's written-off, gathered by the older man, Jakobus
Each reads a different layer — Naila the documents/system, Frik the lie in the room, the polyglot the tongue, the face-reader the body
Naila clocks that the lease documents don't add up — a too-clean ledger, a survey with a predetermined conclusion
Establish Jakobus from outside: the man who sees people, who gathered them when no one else did; warm, watchful, off his own ground
chapters.turn: Naila finds the survey's conclusion was written before the survey began — the data is theatre
chapters.threads: NODE: the crew (series constant) established as secondary POV; the lie in the documents planted; Jakobus seen from outside.

chapters.title: The Welcome Cup
chapters.setting: Batu's ger; present day
beats: The ger welcome: Tuyaa brings the crew to her father Batu's ger; the hospitality of the felt home

PAYOFF #2 — the tea that beats him: süütei tsai, the welcome cup; Jakobus, who eats and drinks everything, is undone by the salt where his body wants sweet and the butter turning on his tongue; he owns it as HIS limit, laughing, never insulting the host — and the failing earns him the fire
The airag by the door he gently declines (no alcohol) — handled with grace, distinct from the tea that beats him
Batu reads Tuyaa: the daughter who left, come back wearing the city's clothes and the mine's brief; the ache between them, unspoken
chapters.turn: Jakobus's honest failure at the cup makes Batu trust him in a way the survey's smoothness never could — the first crack in the visiting master
chapters.threads: PAYOFF #2 (tea). Batu (elder) established; the father-daughter wound opened; Jakobus's first humbling.

chapters.title: What the Survey Can't See
chapters.setting: the open pasture; present day
beats: Batu reads the sky, the grass, the water — judging when and where to move — in a way the survey's instruments and the consultancy's 'empty' map cannot
Tuyaa, the trained scientist, watches her father's read beat her data and feels the old knowledge reclaim her
The crew is let a little way in: the migration timed to grass and water (2-4 moves a year; the otor); the five snouts as wealth-and-kin
First mention of the spring — the only year-round water for the district — and that the drilling has started near it
chapters.turn: Tuyaa's instruments agree with her father's sky-read to the hour — the 'empty frontier' is the most precisely known land she's ever stood on, and she helped call it empty
chapters.threads: NODE: first sight of the wonder. The wonder (sky/migration/water) grounded; the spring planted as the coming wound.

chapters.title: The Blurted Truth
chapters.setting: the fixer's presentation at the sum centre; present day
beats: The fixer makes his case to the district: jobs, GDP, a poor nation that needs the copper; the steppe as frontier; the herders as a past that must make way
His argument has teeth — the herders ARE poor, the law IS on his side — the book refuses to make him stupid
Frik's Tourette's blurt names the polite lie out loud at the exact moment it can't be taken back (the anti-paintover made flesh) — rendered with full dignity, never for comedy
The room's reaction; Tuyaa's flinch of recognition; the fixer's smooth recovery
chapters.turn: Frik's blurt cracks the fixer's frame open in public — and the crew sees the herders are being read out of their own country by a map and a law
chapters.threads: NODE: the flattening force, full-faced. The fixer's real argument; Frik's gift; the law named as the true antagonist.

chapters.title: A Man Who Can Handle Himself
chapters.setting: a local Naadam / district gathering; present day
beats: A local Naadam / district celebration: wrestling, the long-song, airag, the deel — the living culture, not the postcard
The herders quietly check the visitors out — watch them eat, take a joke, carry themselves — and clock Jakobus as a man who can handle himself (true)
The young regional bokh champion introduced with full dignity — half Jakobus's fuss and twice his craft, a title earned at Naadam
The eagle-dance (devekh) ritual before the bouts; the open contest on bare grass; build the anticipation
chapters.turn: A friendly bout is offered to Jakobus in the spirit of welcome and testing — and, off his own ground and a half-step too sure, he accepts like he's the dangerous one in the ring
chapters.threads: NODE: the contest (setup). The champion established; the Naadam wonder; the stage set for the humbling.

chapters.title: His Ground
chapters.setting: the wrestling ground; present day
beats: PAYOFF #1 — the wrestling humbling: Jakobus, who forgot his own creed (defer; you are the student here), is comprehensively, almost gently destroyed by the champion — the champion's grammar, not his; no SF combative saves him
He lands on his back in the dust in front of everyone, the breath gone, the legend briefly nothing
The grace: he laughs at himself, gets up, bows to the better man, makes NO excuses — the locked line: 'On my ground I'd have given him a game. This is his ground. He gave me a lesson.'
The district trusts and loves him MORE for the loss; the champion's quiet respect; Tuyaa watches the master made a student
chapters.turn: The loss, owned without excuse, buys Jakobus and the crew a place at the district's fire that no survey or travelogue ever could
chapters.threads: PAYOFF #1 (wrestling) — the strand's sharpest beat. Champion rendered with dignity; the humility engine at full.

chapters.title: No Brakes
chapters.setting: the camp; the horse lines; present day
beats: PAYOFF #3 — the horse he won't trust: on the most horse-defined ground on earth, the wheel-man's flat distrust of a thing with no brakes that bites; he says so deadpan, drives anything with wheels but won't sit a horse for himself
His own dry telling (once): the open gate, the cattle gone walkabout, 'I'll drive anything you've got with wheels; I don't trust a thing without brakes, and this one bites'
The generous flip side: he won't ride for himself but is first to catch and saddle a horse for whoever's joy it is — the children — 'go on, ride'
The horsed herders find the wheel-man's distrust quietly funny and like him MORE for owning it; keep it distinct from the wrestling, light
chapters.turn: The thing Jakobus won't do for himself, he does gladly for the children — the man who reads a delight that isn't his and gives it away
chapters.threads: PAYOFF #3 (horse / machine creed). Distinct from the wrestling; the Sawubona + giving doctrine in one beat.

chapters.title: The Stone on the Cairn
chapters.setting: the ovoo at the pass; the migration country; present day
beats: The crew let further in: a companion taught to circle the ovoo three times clockwise, add a stone, leave an offering — the threshold shown, the sacred content withheld (MYTHOS Rule 1)
Batu's relationship to the land as obligation, not ownership — he asks before he takes
Jakobus models the withholding: he'd circle the cairn correctly and ASK, not perform — the one place his instinct ports cleanly
Tuyaa feels the gap between the consultancy's 'land as asset' and her father's 'land as kin' — the two ledgers describing the same ground
chapters.turn: Tuyaa understands the survey isn't measuring the land wrong — it's measuring the wrong thing entirely, and she's the one holding the tape
chapters.threads: NODE: the sacred (withheld) + the relay deepens. The two-ledgers theme dramatised; Jakobus's deference as competence.

chapters.title: The Drying Spring
chapters.setting: the sacred spring near the drill site; present day
beats: The discovery: the year-round spring — the only water for the district, and sacred — is going dry where the drilling started (the real Bor Ovoo / Undai pattern)
Naila's documents and Tuyaa's hydrology converge: the mine's water draw is killing the spring, and the survey was built to not see it
Batu's grief, held: the water his grandfather drank, the water the herd needs, the water the ovoo marks — all on the mine's meter
The crew's first wrong instinct stirs: expose it, file it, tell the world FOR them
chapters.turn: The spring is dying on the mine's meter, the survey was designed to miss it, and the crew wants to charge in and save the day — exactly the wrong move
chapters.threads: NODE: the wound revealed (water). The grounded antagonist mechanism; the humility beat set up.

chapters.title: Not Ours to Tell
chapters.setting: the survey camp; a tense crew council; present day
beats: The humility beat (the crew's): their instinct to help/tell/fix proves wrong — going public on the herders' behalf would put words in their mouths, trip the 'outsiders stirring up the natives' frame, and cost the locals control
Jakobus, who sees it first, doesn't lecture — he sits with it, gives something away, lets them arrive at it
The hardest lesson named in action: get out of the way; the unheard are the experts; the telling can only be GIVEN, never taken
Tuyaa caught between: the only one who can translate the herders' undefendable knowledge into the law's language — if she chooses to, and at THEIR direction
chapters.turn: The crew swallows the urge to save the day and learns the real job is to witness and stand guard — and Tuyaa realises the choice is hers alone
chapters.threads: NODE: the humility beat (crew + Tuyaa). The keel dramatised; sets up Act III's hand-back.

chapters.title: The Ones Already Gone
chapters.setting: a neighbour's abandoned winter camp; the road toward the city; present day
beats: The fear of loss, shown: a neighbour family already broken by the last dzud, half-gone to Ulaanbaatar; the empty winter shelter, the sold-off herd
Tuyaa's own wound opens fully: this is why SHE left; she didn't escape the loss, she carried it differently
The city glimpsed through her memory: the ger districts, the smoke, the felt home become a smoke trap — the same dwelling, the life gone out of it
Jakobus rhymes — present, unhurried, not fixing the grief; a quiet thing given away; the man who lost his own world and still carries it
chapters.turn: Tuyaa sees that the city she fled to is where the steppe goes to die, and that her father is being pushed down the same road — and she can't stay neutral
chapters.threads: NODE: the loss (fear-of-loss heart). Tuyaa's wound; the city/dzud as the slow and fast versions of loss; Jakobus's rhyme.

chapters.title: A Thousand Fires
chapters.setting: a long-song night at the camp; present day
beats: THE FIRE — the dance grace-note (§7b): a long-song (urtiin duu) night, the grandmother carrying the song, the morin khuur; the celebration that empties the fear out so people can rest
Jakobus joins the grandmother's circle — WITH them, on their ground, one quiet earned grace-note; never performing AT them; never re-staging the Egypt aria
The cumulative retro-proof: the man who really has been at a thousand fires; joy as resistance, danced one more night against everything taking the steppe
A completed Sawubona/Sikhona-style recognition seeded if earned — a companion who's absorbed the ethos meeting his eye
chapters.turn: For one night the loss is bearable, and Jakobus is, again, the proof that you can lose your world and still dance in someone else's — the grace before the storm
chapters.threads: THE FIRE (dance payoff, §7b). The sacred withheld (fictional long-song). Tonal high point before the midpoint turn.

chapters.title: Strategic Site
chapters.setting: the sum centre; the survey office; present day
beats: Midpoint turn: the mine moves — a 'strategic site' designation / a fence extension / the spring diversion accelerates
The law becomes the real antagonist: pastureland is state-owned, herders hold use-right not title, they cannot refuse, the state can exclude them (the lock the book turns)
The travelogue and the survey Tuyaa was hired for are about to be the instruments that grease it — her name on the report
The fixer offers Tuyaa a way up and out: deliver the clean report, name your price, leave the steppe behind for good
chapters.turn: Tuyaa is handed the pen that will sign her father's pasture away — and a future in the city if she uses it — and has to choose which language she speaks
chapters.threads: NODE: midpoint — the law as antagonist; Tuyaa's choice forced. Act II→III hinge.

chapters.title: Which Tongue
chapters.setting: Batu's ger; the steppe at night; present day
beats: Tuyaa chooses her father's country: she turns her city-fluency on the mine — but FOR the herders and at their direction
The scene with Batu: not a speech, a choice shown; the daughter who left, choosing; the father who won't ask her to stay, seeing her
She does not save them — she gives them the megaphone and steps back; the plan is the district's, the voice is the district's
The crew falls in behind her and the herders: witnesses and guards, not leaders
chapters.turn: Tuyaa refuses to sign and commits to translating the herders' knowledge into the law's language — on their terms, with the camera in their hands
chapters.threads: NODE: the choice / hand-back begins. Tuyaa's arc turns; the keel (locals lead) enacted.

chapters.title: The District Decides
chapters.setting: a gathering of the herder families; present day
beats: The locals take the telling back: Batu and the district lead the defence — the ovoo, the spring, the migration route as the ground they will not yield
The young champion becomes the district's spine — the one who stays and fights with his body and his standing
The grandmother and the song: the future being handed on (a grandchild learning the long-song) even as the fight is joined
The strategy is theirs; the crew's role defined — Naila's document-read, the polyglot's bridge, Jakobus's guard — all SERVING the herders' own move
chapters.turn: The herders commit to a plan of their own making to defend the spring and the route — and the outsiders take their places at the edges, not the centre
chapters.threads: NODE: the locals lead (the relay's point). The win is being built by the experts; the crew witnesses and guards.

chapters.title: The Fence and the Herd
chapters.setting: the contested migration route; the fence line; present day
beats: Rising action: the mine moves to close the route ahead of the herd's seasonal migration; the fence vs. the animals that must reach winter pasture
A dzud is forecast closing in — the killing winter as the clock; if the herd can't reach shelter, it dies
The herders' counter-move, led by the champion and Batu; the crew standing guard; the fixer's muscle on the line
Naila races the paperwork: the document-trail that proves the survey was rigged and the spring is dying on the mine's meter
chapters.turn: The herd must cross the fenced route before the dzud hits, the mine means to stop them, and the proof Naila needs is about to be buried
chapters.threads: NODE: rising action (the route/the dzud clock). The grounded set-piece building; stakes physical and real.

chapters.title: The Wheels He Trusts
chapters.setting: a night drive across the steppe; present day
beats: Jakobus's transferable competence pays off: a hard night drive to get the herders' testimony and Naila's evidence to where it can't be buried — the wheels he trusts, the one machine that obeys him
Contrast with the horse he won't trust: here the wheel-man is in his element, calm under load, the field discipline that ports
The cold is HIS element (SSOT inversion): unlike the desert that beats him, the steppe winter is the one place his mastery holds — banked-fire body-heat, calm in the freeze
But it's the herders' testimony and the herders' voice in the recording — he's the driver, not the hero; the win stays theirs
chapters.turn: The evidence and the herders' own testimony get through — carried, not led, by the outsider — just as the dzud's first wind hits
chapters.threads: NODE: Jakobus's real value (the road). His competence serves, never leads; the cold-ports-here contrast paid off.

chapters.title: The Killing Wind
chapters.setting: the steppe in the dzud; the herd on the route; present day
beats: The dzud hits — white/iron dzud, -40s, the herd strung out on the contested route; the arithmetic of loss made real and immediate
The herders fight to bring the animals through; the champion's strength and standing; Batu's read of the storm; the crew guarding the line
The mine's muscle forced to choose between the fence and human lives in the storm; the fixer's frame cracking against the reality
Loss is real — not everything is saved (the honest record); but the herders' knowledge of the land is what carries the bulk of the herd through where no instrument could
chapters.turn: The herd is brought through — at a cost — by the herders reading the killing land the way no survey ever could; the steppe itself indicts the 'empty frontier' lie
chapters.threads: NODE: the set-piece climax (grounded). The dzud as the proof of the wonder; loss real; the herders' expertise the win.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.setting: the determination / the press / the sum centre; present day
beats: The herders' voice on the record: Tuyaa's translation of their knowledge into the law's and the press's language lands — at their direction, in their words
The rigged survey exposed; the dying spring documented; the fixer's frame fails in public — beaten on dignity and truth, not by being made stupid
The legal reality stays hard: use-right, not title; the win is partial, contested, real — a route kept open / the spring defended / the determination held, not a clean rescue
Frik's truth and Naila's documents and the polyglot's bridge all in service of the herders' own win
chapters.turn: The herders win the thing they fought for — modest, partial, theirs — and the outsiders' only credit is having handed back the megaphone
chapters.threads: NODE: the win (culture handed on, not saved). Honest/partial per the real record; hope not triumph.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Chose
chapters.setting: Batu's ger; the steppe; present day
beats: The father-daughter resolution, shown not spoken: Batu and Tuyaa, the leaving and the choosing reconciled; she belongs again to a country and a father
Tuyaa's vindication is not the city's approval — it's the thing she was taught to leave behind; she will use both her tongues for the steppe
The grandchild and the long-song; the herd carried through; the future handed on, not mourned — the grip, not the grave
The cost acknowledged: the dzud and the city and the law don't vanish; the people are still fighting, still here, still expert
chapters.turn: Tuyaa stays — or leaves changed — the daughter who chose her father's country; the loss carried, not erased
chapters.threads: NODE: Tuyaa's resolution (the heart). The fear-of-loss discipline: hope not certainty; culture handed on.

chapters.title: The Road On
chapters.setting: the camp at dawn; the road out; present day
beats: Jakobus and the crew leave — the Sawubona lesson carried, the next unheard place ahead; the road, never the lead
A completed Sawubona/Sikhona-style recognition lands if earned: a companion who's absorbed the ethos answering his eye — without ever explaining it
The crew changed: the band of the written-off who learned, place by place, not to do to anyone what was done to them
The camera last on the herders and the steppe, not the visitors — the felt and the sky, the home that moves, going on
chapters.turn: The visitors go, carrying the lesson; the steppe stays, expert and alive and still under threat — the unheard, heard for once
chapters.threads: NODE: the road pulls onward (series spine). The camera stays with the unheard; the crew's arc; Jakobus the road.

chapters.title: The Felt and the Sky — A Note on the Real Places
chapters.setting: n/a
beats: Author's note + gazetteer: separate real/visitable (Naadam; Mongolian-owned herder-stay tourism; urtiin duu & khoomei as UNESCO heritage; the real dzud record; the documented Oyu Tolgoi/Khanbogd water-and-pasture case) from contested (Genghis historiography; the figures flagged in PLACE_RESEARCH) from invented/composited (the district, the mine, all characters, the spring/route)

Binding sensitivity-reader note: read by Mongolian cultural advisors before publication; no sacred content depicted; the Khalkha Mongol steppe-herders are distinct from the Kazakh eagle-hunters of Bayan-Olgii — named, not conflated
Pointer to Mongolian-owned herder-stay tourism and the herders' own organisations (the series' tourism-dignity payoff)
The dedication and the series keel: the unheard are the experts; their story can only be given, never spoken for
chapters.turn: The candour that makes the wonder trustworthy and the respect real
chapters.threads: Back matter (binding — STORY_BIBLE/PLOT). The tourism-dignity payoff; the sensitivity gate stated in the book itself.
